title: End of an outward allocation pass
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a,B\in\mathbb{N}$, and choose a schedule-symbol input, a base configuration on it, a valid input-head position $p$, an integer budget-head position $b$, and budget and guide tapes $\beta$ and $\gamma$. For either direction, one step from the corresponding phase of allocation index $0$, with unary head at $B+1$ over the unary tape with $B$ markers and guide head at $g$, enters the right-edge phase for the rightward pass or the left-edge phase for the leftward pass. The unary head stays at $B+1$, the guide head moves one cell in the pass direction, and the guide tape is updated to carry an interior mark at its former head position $g$.
hypotheses_covered: W is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
a and B are natural numbers
base is a configuration on the chosen input
p is a valid input-head position
b and g are integer head positions
bt and gt are controller tapes
replaced:
From layout phase $0$ (of either direction) with unary head at cell $B+1$ --- the
blank cell terminating the unary tape with $B$ markers --- and guide head at cell $g$,
one step writes an interior mark at guide cell $g$, moves the guide head one further
cell outward, keeps the unary head in place, and enters the right-edge or left-edge
phase according to the direction.
